title: The Waymo effect
summary: Craig Piercycpiercy@ans.org The focus of the September issue of Nuclear News issue is on new technology, and the stories within are reflective of the broader wave of innovation sweeping the industry—a wave driven in no small part by the head-jerking progress of AI and its pervasion into our economy and way of life. Something caught my eye a few days ago: an ad by Waymo touting its careful intentionality in deploying its fleet of driverless vehicles in the U.S. “Now, the Waymo driver is safer than a human one,” says the soothing female voiceover, “statistically 10 times safer in the cities we serve.” It made me realize that most if not all safety-related applications of AI will at some point— usually after a lot of trial and error—reach a state of “too good to not use.” At that point, people become the weakest link in the safety chain. While the first Waymo ride can be a cognitively dissonant experience, I think we will be surprised at how easily we will all get used to seeing the road ahead behind an empty driver’s seat, assuming the safety case holds up.

title: Kairos and Samsung C&T partner up on Hermes 2
summary: Earlier this week, Kairos Power announced a binding term sheet signed with Samsung C&T Engineering and Construction Group that will facilitate the two companies’ collaboration on Kairos’s Hermes 2 demonstration plant on multiple fronts. The terms of that agreement include Samsung C&T providing up to $100 million to Kairos through a combination of direct investment and in-kind engineering services for the project. To that end, Samsung C&T also has officially joined Kairos’s engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) team to support both the delivery of Hermes 2 and future deployments of Kairos’s reactor technology.

title: Fuel decladding skid ready to deploy at INL’s Moran test bed
summary: A mobile skid designed to process and remove the cladding from spent nuclear fuel has been declared ready for use at Idaho National Laboratory’s Moran Nuclear Fuels Test Facility. Production of the skid was funded by the Athena Initiative, a project that the National Nuclear Security Administration’s Nonproliferation Stewardship Program began in 2022 to support nonproliferation efforts in the United States.
